title: Cyber Insurance Adoption Declines Among French SMEs, 45% Now Uncovered
content_md:
Cyber insurance adoption is declining among French SMEs. According to Hiscox, 45% of French small and medium enterprises now have no cyber coverage, up from 39% in 2025. The share of SMEs with a dedicated cyber policy dropped from 33.6% to 27.6% in one year.

The average financial impact of a cyberattack on French SMEs over the past 12 months reached $50,489 (approximately EUR 45,900). Payment fraud through diverted transactions was the most common consequence, affecting 40% of attacked firms. Human error was involved in 26% of incidents, primarily through phishing and social engineering. 66.8% of incidents caused less than one day of disruption, but the average outage across all incidents reached 24.5 hours.

96% of French SMEs that suffered an attack said it affected their strategy or financial position, with growth delays cited in 36% of cases, impact on company valuation in 33%, and postponed technology investments in 31%. On the workforce side, 37% of employees in affected companies reported high stress levels, 27% reported degraded workplace atmosphere, and 25% of companies saw increased sick leave. Nearly half of French decision-makers (49%) consider data poisoning the most significant emerging cyber threat over the next five years.
